 JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 13-09-2024 at about 3.10 p.m., the petitioner was the conductor in the APSRTC bus bearing Reg. No.AP-03-Z- 5419, proceeding from Tirupathi to Bengaluru.

When the said bus was near Mogili Ghat, Bangarupalem Mandalam, on Chittoor-Palamaner NH-69 road, Chittoor District, Andhrapradesh, at that time one Tata Goods carriage container lorry bearing Reg. No.AP-15-TB-7777, came from the opposite direction i.e.
Palamaner towards Chittoor side, the same being driven by its driver with high speed,
in a rash and negligent manner and due to excess speed lost control over his vehicle and dashed against the bus of the deceased.
Due to said impact, the said bus got dashed to another lorry bearing Reg. No.AP-03-TE-7619, which was behind the bus.
As a result of which, the petitioner has sustained grievous multiple injuries and five passengers traveling in the said bus and the bus driver died on the spot.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital, Chittoor,
wherein he took first aid treatment and then he was shifted to Christian Medical College, Vellore, Ranipet Campus, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient.

3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 did not choose to appear and remained absent.

Hence, the respondent No.1 is placed as ex-parte.
4.
The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has contended that, three vehicles are involved in the alleged accident, but the petitioner has not made the owners and insurers of APSRTC bus bearing No.AP-03-Z-5419 and lorry bearing No.AP-03-TE-7619 as parties to the present petition.
The respective owners and insurers of the said vehicles are necessary parties to the claim petition and the petition is liable to be dismissed for non-joinder of necessary parties.
Further it is contended that, the petition is filed beyond the limitation period and no proper, cogent reasons have been assigned to condone the delay in filing the claim petition.
Hence, the claim petition is liable to be dismissed.

Further it is contended that,
the alleged accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving on the part of the drivers of all the three vehicles.
If the drivers of all the three vehicles were careful and vigilant, they could have avoided the accident.
The contributory negligence is more on the part of drivers of APSRTC bus and lorry bearing No.AP-03-TE-7619.
Unauthorized passengers were traveling in lorry bearing No.AP-03-TE-7619 and to get compensation to them a false case has been filed only against the driver of lorry bearing No.AP-15-TB-7777.
If any compensation is to be paid, it is to be paid by the owners and insurers of APSRTC bus and lorry bearing No.AP-03-TE-7619.
Further it is contended that, the petition is bad for non-compliance of provision under Section 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.

Further it is contended that, the liability of this respondent if any is subject to terms and conditions and limitations of insurance policy and provisions of Motor Vehicle Act, if policy is issued in favour of the owner of container lorry bearing Reg. No.AP-15-TB-7777.
Further it is contended that, the driver of the lorry bearing No.AP-15- TB-7777 was driving the same without possessing a valid and effective driving licence, fitness certificate and permit.
Hence, there is a violation of policy conditions, rules and regulations of Motor Vehicle Act.
Hence, this respondent is not liable to pay compensation and not liable to indemnify the owner of the said vehicle.

Further it is contended that,
the petitioner should strictly prove that, there is no fault on the part of the drivers of APSRTC bus and lorry bearing No.AP-03-TE-7619.

It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner,
injuries sustained, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
The compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
For the above denials and contentions, it prayed for dismissal of the petition.

sentences.text: 11. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 11, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending lorry bearing No.AP-15-TB-7777.

Due to excess speed the driver of said lorry lost control over his vehicle, jumped the median road divider, went to other lane and dashed to the APSRTC bus bearing Reg. No.AP-03-Z-5419 of the deceased, which was proceeding in the opposite direction.
Due to said impact the said APSRTC bus turned around and dashed against the lorry bearing No.AP-03-TE-7619.

Due to said collision, the accused/driver of offending lorry, the driver of APSRTC bus and 5 passengers in the said bus have died on the spot and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries all over the body in the said accident.

The investigation officer in his final report/charge-sheet, which is marked as Ex.P.11, has clearly stated that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending lorry bearing No.AP-15-TB-7777.
12.

At the outset, is it pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
the issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 in respect of offending lorry bearing No.AP-15-TB-7777 and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

Further, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners has remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/Respondent No.1, as he did not choose to appear and contest the case of the petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.2/insurer of offending vehicle has specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the alleged accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent driving of the drivers of the APSRTC bus bearing No.AP-03-Z-5419 and lorry bearing No.AP-03-TE- 7619 and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry bearing Reg. No.AP-15-TB-7777.
But, it has failed to establish the said contentions.
The respondent No.2 has neither adduced any evidence, nor produced any document to establish the above contentions.
Even it has not stepped into witness box to depose the said contentions on oath.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending lorry bearing No.AP-15-TB-7777 and dashing the same to the APSRTC bus bearing No.AP-03-Z-5419, proceeding on the other lane in the opposite direction.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been brought out from his mouth, which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which establishes that the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the APSRTC bus bearing No.AP-03-Z-5419 or driver of lorry bearing No.AP-03-TE-7619 or there was any contributory negligence on their part in the cause of accident.

13. Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazar and Ex.P.4 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place in the middle of the road, on Chittoor-Palamaner NH-69 road, at Mogili Ghat,
Bangarupalem Mandal, Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh, in between the offending lorry bearing No.AP-15- TB-7777 and APSRTC bus bearing No.AP-03-Z-5419 and lorry bearing No.AP-15-TB-7619,
proceeding on the other lane of National highway road in the opposite direction.

Further it is pertinent to note, as per Ex.P.7 Motor Vehicle Accident report, the accident has not occurred due to Chiranjeevi P vs Sudhakar Babu G on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110520912/

When the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the drivers of the APSRTC bus bearing No.AP-03-Z-5419 and lorry bearing No.AP-15-TB-7619, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that,
the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.
Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.11 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry bearing Reg.
No.AP-15-TB-7777 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged by the driver or the owner of offending vehicle.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, with regard to date, time and place of accident,
involvement of the offending lorry bearing Reg. No.AP-15- TB-7777 in the said accident, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to petitioner in the said accident.

14. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.8 wound certificate and Ex.P.17 discharge summary, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.

He has suffered 1) right open shaft of humerus fracture, 2) right sided mandible fracture,
3) right sided displaced maxillary fracture, 4) right side posterior aspect multiple undisplaced rib fractures (6-11), 5) right mild hemothorax, 6) liver injury - grade 3, 6) minimal hemoperitoneum and 7) thoracic spine transverse process fractures (T8 - T11).
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that, the above medical records produced by the petitioner are false documents.

15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

on Chittoor-Palamaner NH-69 road, at Mogili Ghat, Bangarupalem Mandal, Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the TATA Goods Carriage Container lorry bearing Reg. No.AP- 15-TB-7777.

sentences.text: Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending lorry bearing Reg. No.AP-15-TB-7777 and he has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

As per the medical records placed on record by the petitioner, he has sustained 1)
right open shaft of humerus fracture, 2) right sided mandible fracture, 3) right sided displaced maxillary fracture, 4) right side posterior aspect multiple undisplaced rib fractures (6- 11), 5) right mild hemothorax, 6) liver injury - grade 3, 6) minimal hemoperitoneum and 7) thoracic spine transverse process fractures (T8 - T11).
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non-pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock,
loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
19. Towards loss of future income:
The petitioner has deposed that, earlier to the accident, he was working as APSRTC bus conductor and was getting monthly salary of Rs.42,408/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
But, the petitioner has neither produced any document nor he has examined the doctor to establish that, due to injuries sustained in the accident he has suffered any physical disability or deformity.

The petitioner has failed to prove that, due to accidental injuries he has suffered any physical disability and he is not in a position to continue his avocation or perform his regular work and thereby, he has lost his earning capacity.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding compensation under head loss of future income due to permanent physical disability does not arise at all.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head of loss of future income due to disability.
20. Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.5,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has not produced any medical bills or prescriptions.
Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head of medical expenses.

21. Pain and sufferings: In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e. 1) right open shaft of humerus fracture, 2) right sided mandible fracture,
3) right sided displaced maxillary fracture, 4) right side posterior aspect multiple undisplaced rib fractures (6-11), 5) right mild hemothorax, 6) liver injury - grade 3, 6) minimal hemoperitoneum and 7) thoracic spine transverse process fractures (T8 - T11).
As per Ex.P.17 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 13 days from 14-09-2024 to 26-09-2024, in Christian Medical College, Vellore.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into consideration the injuries sustained by the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, compensation amount of Rs.80,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.

sentences.text: Attendant charges:
As per Ex.P.17 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 13 days in Christian Medical College, Vellore.
He might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during the said period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 13 = Rs.13,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
23. Food and nourishment:
As per Ex.P.17 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 13 days in Christian Medical College, Vellore.
He might have spent considerable amount towards food and nourishment during the said period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.800 x 13 = Rs.10,400/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
24. Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Chitipiralla, Chittoor District,
Andhrapradesh, the accident has occurred on Chittoor-Palamaner NH-69 road, at Mogili Ghat,
Bangarupalem Mandal, Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh and he has taken treatment at Christian Medical College, Vellore.
Taking into consideration the distance in between the above places, compensation of Rs.10,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
25. Loss of income during treatment period:

The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working as APSRTC bus conductor and was getting monthly salary of Rs.42,408/-
per month.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do work and continue his avocation.

To substantiate the same, he has produced department identity card, conductor licence, leave sanction letter and salary slips for the month of June to August - 2024, which are marked as Ex.P.13 to 16.
The said documents clearly establishes that, as on the date of accident the petitioner was working as APSRTC bus conductor and at present he is continued in the said job.
As per the Ex.P.16 salary slips, for the month of June to August- 2024, the petitioner was drawing gross salary of Rs.46,818/- per month.
After deducting professional tax of Rs.200/-, the net salary of the petitioner will be Rs.46,618/- per month.

Further,
as per Ex.P.15 leave sanction letter, the petitioner has availed special disability leave for the period from 15- 12-2024 to 15-03-2026 for a period of 15 months.

Further, the petitioner has clearly stated in his cross-examination that, he has availed medical leave for 18 months and during the said period for 3 months he has drawn full salary and for remaining period he is paid half salary.
But, the petitioner has not produced any document show that, he is paid half salary for 15 months of total medical leave period.
In absence of evidence with respect to same, there is no other option left before this Court, except to hold that, there is no loss of income to the petitioner during the treatment period.
Therefore, the question of awarding compensation to the petitioner towards loss of income during the treatment period does not arise at all.
Hence, no compensation is awarded under this particular head.
26. Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 37 years and unfortunately he has suffered grievous injuries in the said accident and undergone treatment for 13 days as in-patient in Christian Medical College,
Vellore.
Further, he might have taken rest for about two months.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards loss of amenities during the said period would be just and reasonable.

sentences.text: Future medical expenses:
The petitioner has neither adduced any evidence nor he has produced any document to show that, he requires to undergo any further treatment for the injuries sustained in the accident.
Therefore, in such circumstances, the question of awarding compensation for future medical expenses does not arise at all.
Hence, no compensation is awarded under this particular head.

28. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows:
1. Loss of future income Rs. -Nil- 2.
Medical expenses -Nil- 3. Pain and sufferings 80,000-00 4. Attendant charges 13,000-00 5. Food and nourishment 10,400-00 6.
Conveyance expenses 10,000-00 7. Loss of income during -Nil- treatment period 8. Loss of amenities 30,000-00
9. Future medical expenses -Nil-
In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,43,400/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
29. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending lorry bearing No.AP-15-TB-7777.

Further, the insurance policy bearing No.3379/04006662/000/00, issued by the respondent No.2,
in respect of offending lorry bearing No.AP-15-TB-7777 was valid from 02-08-2024 to 01-08-2025.
As such, the said policy was valid as on the date of accident i.e. 13-09-2024.
There is no evidence on record to show that, there is any breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy by the insured/respondent No.1.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending lorry bearing No.AP-15-TB-7777, the accident has occurred and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.

Therefore, the respondent Chiranjeevi P vs Sudhakar Babu G on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110520912/
9 No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,43,400/-,
with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization, from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
30. Issue No.3:

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.1,43,400/- (Rupees one lakh forty three thousand four hundred only), with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the said amount within two months from the date of this order.
Entire compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment, on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Due to said collision, the accused/driver of offending lorry, the driver of APSRTC bus and 5 passengers in the said bus have died on the spot and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries all over the body in the said accident.
Whereas, the respondent No.2/insurer of offending vehicle has specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the alleged accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent driving of the drivers of the APSRTC bus bearing No.AP-03-Z-5419 and lorry bearing No.AP-03-TE- 7619 and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry bearing Reg. No.AP-15-TB-7777.
When the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the drivers of the APSRTC bus bearing No.AP-03-Z-5419 and lorry bearing No.AP-15-TB-7619, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that,
the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.
Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.11 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry bearing Reg.
No.AP-15-TB-7777 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged by the driver or the owner of offending vehicle.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, with regard to date, time and place of accident,
involvement of the offending lorry bearing Reg. No.AP-15- TB-7777 in the said accident, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to petitioner in the said accident.
15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."
16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.
